old_title: Iran war latest: Trump claims control of Hormuz as he demands Iran pay for US deaths
new_title: Iran war live: US fires on ship for defying blockade as Trump claims Hormuz control
old_text:
Donald Trump says the US Navy has cleared mines from the Strait of Hormuz and now has "100 per cent" control of the key waterway, which Iran says will remain closed until Washington meets its demands.
Trump told reporters in the Oval Office: "It's open now," claiming the US was "the only one that has control of the Strait of Hormuz right now".
Trump, meanwhile, demanded war compensation from Iran on Monday in a shocking reversal of the six-point ultimatum presented to Washington as Tehran's conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran's top security official said earlier that they would allow traffic to pass through the key channel only once the US meets six terms, including "payment in full" for damage inflicted during the war.
But Trump snubbed the proposal in a message on Truth Social, saying: "It is an interesting idea because now I am likewise demanding compensation from Iran," Trump said, adding: "I have instructed my representatives to put this firmly into any, and all, future negotiations."
Trump secretly switched planes to leave Turkey due to Iran assassination threat
US president Donald Trump was secretly transported away from last month's Nato summit in Ankara, Turkey, using a secondary military plane while an elaborate deception made it seem he was aboard Air Force One, according to a report published by The Washington Post on Monday.
The newspaper reported that the covert movement was triggered by an assassination threat from Iran targeting Mr Trump. Reporters and several White House personnel were left believing they were travelling on the same aircraft as the president as his return journey to Washington commenced following the annual gathering of Nato leaders.
The newspaper based its account on reviewed documentation, a US official aware of the operation and another individual familiar with the president's travel arrangements.
Who are Iran's new wartime commanders?
Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei has appointed six senior commanders to key military and security posts, reshaping the wartime leadership after several top commanders were killed.
The appointments came a day after former IRGC chief Mohsen Rezaee was named secretary of the Supreme National Security Council.
- Ali Abdollahi: Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces, overseeing coordination across the military.
- Kioumars Heydari: Deputy Chief of Staff.
- Ahmad Vahidi: New IRGC commander, tasked with boosting deterrence and readiness for "powerful offensive operations".
- Mostafa Izadi: Vahidi's deputy, responsible for operational readiness.
- Ali Ozmaei: New IRGC Navy commander, a key role amid tensions around the Strait of Hormuz.
- Hossein Taeb: New Basij commander, focusing on mobilisation and domestic intelligence. Basij is Iran's paramilitary volunteer militia within the IRGC.
British couple jailed in Iran over espionage end their hunger strike
British couple Craig and Lindsay Foreman, who have been jailed in Iran on widely criticised espionage charges, have ended hunger strikes lasting 93 and 84 days respectively.
The East Sussex couple, who deny the charges, were arrested in January last year while travelling by motorcycle from Europe to Australia and sentenced to 10 years in prison in February.
Craig Foreman's sentence was later reportedly extended after he spoke to the media.
They began the hunger strike in May after prison authorities stopped them from contacting their families.
They agreed to end it after guards promised they could resume direct contact, though their family said Monday that contact had not yet been restored.
Oil prices rise as US-Iran negotiations over Strait of Hormuz seem to stall
Oil prices rose as US-Iran negotiations over reopening the Strait of Hormuz stalled. Brent climbed to $88 a barrel and US crude to $82.45, both their highest levels since 31 July, after a roughly 5 per cent jump on Monday.
The latest escalation came after Donald Trump rejected Iran's terms for reopening the strait and instead demanded compensation from Tehran, raising fears that the crucial shipping route will remain disrupted.
He later wrote on Truth Social: "Iran should be responsible for the damages and death caused to the people of Lebanon, Syria, Yemen, and Gaza!"
Chuck Schumer attacks Trump over Iran war
US Senate minority leader Chuck Schumer has called Donald Trump's handling of the Iran war a "complete and total failure".
"Donald Trump got us into an illegal war, is losing his illegal war, and has no way out of his illegal war," Schumer wrote on X.
"His lack of strategy, discipline, and any ability to seriously negotiate is endangering our troops and raising prices for everyday Americans," he said.
"Trump's leadership is a complete and total failure. We must end this war and begin to repair the damage he has wrought," he added.
Trump demands war reparations from Iran after Tehran called for compensation
Donald Trump has said he will demand war reparations from Iran for the deaths and injuries of US soldiers and civilians over decades.
He made the demand after Iranian negotiators called for compensation for the destruction caused by the war, which has killed thousands and severely damaged Iran's military and economy.
Trump wrote on Truth Social: "Now I am likewise demanding compensation from Iran, for all of the people that they have killed and gravely wounded with their roadside bombs and many conflicts, for which they are famous, as led initially by Gen Soleimani, including the families of those killed on the USS Cole, and thousands of others killed in combat.
"Additionally, compensation should be paid to the families of the hundreds of thousands of innocent protesters that Iran has killed over the last 50 years, not to mention the 52,000 that have been killed in the last five months."
Catch up: Trump says 'it always works out' as plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz stalls
Donald Trump has declared that it "always works out" as he said the US will scale down the intensity of its efforts to reopen shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
Talks to end their war and reopen shipping through the Strait of Hormuz appeared to have stalled, after Tehran demanded a series of conditions, including the payment of compensation, before it reopens the waterway.
"We are only semi-negotiating with them. We are just watching Iran with its huge inflation and the fact they have no money," he told Axios. "It will work out. It always works out. It's like a chess game."
Tehran is in negotiations with Oman to partially open up the Strait, but set out six conditions the US must meet, including a permanent end to the war and aggression against Iran and its allies in Lebanon, Palestine, Yemen, and Iraq.
Trump used elaborate ruse to fly out of Turkey following summit because of Iran threat - report
Donald Trump secretly switched from Air Force One to a smaller military jet after last month's Nato summit in Turkey amid an Iranian assassination threat, The Washington Post reported.
After publicly boarding an older Air Force One, Trump was reportedly moved via an airport catering truck to an Air Force C-32A and flown to the UK, while journalists were led to believe he remained on Air Force One.
The US has not independently confirmed the report.
"As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats," White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement.
During a gaggle with reporters aboard the aircraft, Trump was asked directly if there was any credible threats on Air Force One by Iran, according to the Associated Press.
"Well, I have a threat all the time. I'm number one on their list before you," Trump said. He added to the travelling reporters, "But if I go, you go."
Iran president says supreme leader shared message of 'unity and cohesion'
Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian has said that Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei had a message of "unity and cohesion" during a recent meeting that lasted seven hours.
Pezeshkian said Khamenei, who hasn't made an appearance since becoming supreme leader, was in perfect health.
On Monday, Khamenei's office announced several key appointments, including the selection of a former wartime commander and veteran political insider to lead the country's highest security body.
new_text:
The US military fired on a Panamanian-flagged ship in the Gulf of Oman yesterday after accusing it of trying to evade the American blockade on Iranian ports.
The military said the vessel had ignored warnings to stop, prompting an American helicopter to fire missiles into the engine room of the M/V Vela Nova, disabling the ship.
Details of the incident emerged as the US president told reporters late on Tuesday night that "we totally control the Strait of Hormuz ... Nobody else, only us". "At some point, maybe they'll do something and then they get blown away," he added of Iran.
Iran was resolute on Tuesday it continued to exert power over the strait, and that the US must end the war before they will allow normal shipping to be restored.
Mohsen Rezaee, the new secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said on social media that the "message is clear" that the strait will remain shut until the US agrees to terms and pulls back.
Earlier this week, Trump snubbed Iran's six conditions for reopening the strait, which included "payment in full" for damage inflicted on Iran throughout the war.
Just 29% of expected midterm voters say they approve of Trump's handling of Iran
A cable TV polling expert claims that numbers from two surveys conducted two years apart show just how deeply President Donald Trump has disappointed America's voters when it comes to Iran.
CNN chief data analyst Harry Enten said Tuesday that a July 2024 poll of people who were extremely motivated to vote in that year's presidential election found that 53 percent were confident Trump would be able to handle the situation in Iran, according to a video clip posted online.
But a July poll of people extremely motivated to vote in November's midterm elections shows that just 29 percent now approve of how Trump is actually handling Iran, Enten said.
"We're talking about a 24-point fall in just two years," he said. "What was an advantage for President Trump going into the 2024 election amongst those who really wanted to turn out and vote has turned into a tremendous disadvantage this time around."
Iranian-backed Houthis kill 6 in attack on vessel
At least six people were killed by Iran-backed Houthi rebels attacking a vessel in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the Yemeni authorities said.
Yemen's coast guard said the dead included four crew members and two members of the government-allied National Resistance Forces.
Houthis fired three ballistic missiles at the Yemeni commercial vessel, according to Yemen's internationally recognised government.
They are the first known deaths from Houthi attacks on shipping off Yemen in the latest bout of fighting in the Arab country.
Drones hit Iranian Kurdish opposition camps
Four drones hit three Iranian Kurdish opposition camps near Erbil in Iraq this morning, with no casualties reported, security sources told Reuters.
Pakistan says three sailors killed in Red Sea attack
At least three Pakistani nationals were killed in an attack on a ship in the Red Sea, the foreign ministry said.
"Pakistan strongly condemns the Houthi attack on a non-combatant commercial vessel," the foreign minister said on X.
The alleged attack comes as Iran-backed Houthis have been accused of increasing attacks on vessels near the waters of Yemen.
Syria says IAEA will announce 'significant progress' on nuclear file
Syria will host a delegation from the International Atomic Energy Agency in the coming days to announce "significant progress" on the issue of nuclear materials, Syria's Atomic Energy Commission said.
Since the ouster of president Bashar al-Assad in late 2024, Syria's new authorities have committed to working with the United Nations' nuclear watchdog to address the legacy of nuclear activities during decades of Assad family rule
Israeli military 'mistakenly' launches interceptor in Lebanon
The Israeli army said an interceptor was mistakenly launched in Southern Lebanon this morning.
The Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) said the interceptor had been launched at a target that was later confirmed to be IDF fire from operations carried out within the Security Zone.
Trump demands reparations from Iran for 'all the people they have killed'
President Donald Trump is demanding that Iran pay compensation to American victims of Iranian-backed attacks as he responds to Tehran's own demand for war reparations.
In a Monday post on Truth Social, Trump said he had "instructed my representatives to put this firmly into any, and all, future negotiations" - casting Iran's compensation demand as a novel idea he was happy to borrow.
More here.
US ambassador claims Iranian regime weakest since 1979
The US ambassador to Israel has claimed that the Iranian regime is the "weakest they have been since they took over in 1979" amid Donald Trump's war on Tehran.
"The operation between the United States and Israel did an enormous level of damage," Mike Huckabee told Newsmax, praising the US president's bid to "bankrupt them".
US fires on ship it said was trying to break blockade of Iran
The US military said that its forces fired on a Panamanian-flagged ship in the Gulf of Oman that tried to evade the American blockade on Iranian ports. The move came as president Donald Trump tries to keep economic pressure on the Islamic Republic.
US Central Command said the vessel had ignored warnings to stop, prompting an American helicopter to fire missiles into the engine room of the M/V Vela Nova, disabling the ship.
The statement did not say whether the ship's crew suffered any casualties.
